implementation: The opt-in path keeps a cached source shadow per frame slot, compares each row, writes sparse runs and falls back to a whole-row write when more than 64 bytes change. Rebind invalidates every shadow so a reset cannot reuse stale ownership data.
interpretation: In this paired dummy-SDL timedemo, dirty-copy reduced average publish time from 4.413 ms to 3.432 ms and increased measured FPS from 28.3 to 29.3, while generating more bounded backpressure. The result is promising but not a release-wide performance pass; the option remains opt-in until static, combat, UI and real-vblank scenes are profiled.
scope: Both runs are real ARM and FPGA execution with software rendering and dummy SDL. Physical HDMI/vblank pacing, speakers, peripherals, zero-underrun audio, deterministic gameplay and approximately 60 FPS qualification remain open.
